title: Cohort-aware exposure orchestrator with multi-metric sequential analysis
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: build an A/B/cohort exposure orchestrator that schedules incremental exposure for new model versions, evaluates a basket of metrics with sequential statistical checks, supports non-invasive shadow traffic, and can auto-rollback on detected regressions. This ticket scopes the cross-team specification, success criteria, and an initial implementation plan for a v0 rollout integrated into Redwood Console's rollout UI and runtime routing. The system must support: cohort-based ramps (by region/product-tier), multi-metric decisioning (latency p95, downstream task F1/semantic similarity, per-token cost), sequential early-stopping rules to limit exposure, and transparent audit logs for regulatory traceability.
acceptance_criteria: Can create an experiment that defines cohorts and a ramp schedule in Console (shadow -> 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20%)
Sequential statistical checks run automatically at each ramp checkpoint and produce a pass/fail/continue decision
Support for multi-metric decisioning with configurable weights and tie-break rules
Auto-rollback trigger that executes within the runtime (fallback to pinned stable variant) when a checkpoint fails the safety gates
Shadow traffic mode available to mirror live traffic for offline metric collection without affecting production responses
Experiment events, decisions, and metric snapshots appear in the rollout timeline and are exportable for audits
End-to-end integration test with synthetic traffic demonstrates early-stopping after simulated regression on p95 latency and semantic score drop

implementation_notes: Exposure sequencing: support shadow -> micro-cohort -> scaled cohorts. Each checkpoint evaluates a windowed sample (configurable units/time) before progressing.

Statistical checks: implement group-sequential test wrapper to allow early stopping with controlled Type I error (alpha-spending). Default spending function: OBrien-Fleming-like aggressiveness configurable per-experiment.

Quality metrics: compute Bayesian posterior for semantic-similarity and response-quality metrics; use posterior probability of degradation > delta as a gate (eg P(degradation > 0.02) > 0.95 triggers fail).
Composite decision: allow weighted aggregation of metrics into a single score; support tie-break precedence (safety metrics > latency > cost).
Cohort balancing: stratify by cohort keys (region, customer tier); run per-cohort checks and a pooled meta-check. Auto-pause if any high-priority cohort fails.
Runtime integration: runtime will provide an API to pause traffic to the variant, switch traffic routing, and record immediate fallback events (ENG-20910 implements runtime switch interface).
Observability: enrich rollout timeline with metric snapshots, confidence intervals, sample sizes; surface recommended action with rationale string for audits.
Experiment reproducibility: store seeds, metric snapshot hashes, and evaluation datasets used for semantic scoring in the experiment artifact store.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Shadow mode for 48h across 100% of traffic (no consumer-visible changes). Collect baseline metrics and per-cohort deltas.
Phase 1: Micro canary 0.1% for 1h -> run sequential checks (latency p95, token cost, semantic score).
Phase 2: Ramp to 1% for 3h -> re-evaluate with extended sample; require pass on primary safety metric and no >5% regression on quality.
Phase 3: Ramp to 5% for 6h -> run pooled and per-cohort checks; if any high-priority cohort fails, pause and rollback.
Phase 4: Ramp to 20% and then to full traffic if all checkpoints pass across 24h windows. Auto-rollback will trigger immediate runtime fallback when a checkpoint fails the hard gate.
Fallback actions: soft-fallback (route new requests to stable variant but continue collecting metrics) and hard-rollback (immediate full switch to stable).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: noisy quality metrics leading to false positives. Mitigation: use Bayesian shrinkage and minimum sample thresholds before decisions.
Risk: divergent cohort behavior (e.g., region-specific regressions). Mitigation: require per-cohort gating for high-sensitivity cohorts and flagging for manual review.
Risk: runtime rollback latencies may be non-zero. Mitigation: implement immediate routing switch API and pre-warmed fallback instances.
Risk: regulatory audit requirements. Mitigation: persist decision rationales, metric snapshots, and actor IDs to the audit log for compliance.
Risk: increased cost from mirroring/shadowing. Mitigation: limit shadow sampling window and reuse cached responses where feasible.
